backlog.spec: In the current train.py, fit_predict blends a descriptor LightGBM rank with a Tanimoto-kernel GP posterior mean on Morgan bits; the GP noise level is picked by choose_sigma2, which runs a 5-fold scaffold-grouped inner CV over sigma2 in {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} and returns the single best value. Selecting one value from three noisy inner-CV scores is unstable. Replace the selection with an average: delete choose_sigma2 (and its now-unused GroupKFold / MurckoScaffold / spearmanr imports if nothing else uses them) and instead compute the GP posterior mean for each sigma2 in a fixed grid of (0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0), rank-transform each resulting test prediction vector (rankdata / n), and average those ranks to form p_fp. Keep everything else identical, including the final 0.6/0.4 rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM. This removes the inner CV, so the job should also get faster.
backlog.title: Average GP posteriors over a sigma2 grid instead of selecting one

backlog.spec: The descriptor LightGBM runs 400 trees at learning_rate 0.03 and only its final iteration is used, so the prediction sits at whatever point 400 rounds happens to land on. Replace the single prediction with a snapshot average: fit the model once as now, then call lgbm.predict(X_test, num_iteration=k) for k in {200, 275, 350, 400}, rank-normalize each of the four prediction vectors, and average them to form p_desc. This costs no extra training time (predictions at truncated iteration counts come from the same fitted booster) and acts as an implicit regularizer against over- or under-shooting the optimal number of rounds on only ~780 training molecules per fold. Keep the GP branch and the 0.6/0.4 final blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble over LightGBM boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Replace the target y = rank/n with a normal score: scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(y)-0.5)/n). Use it for both LightGBM and GP fits. The final outputs are still rank-blended.
backlog.title: Gaussian-rank target transform

backlog.spec: After the first GP prediction on test_smiles, take the test molecules whose predicted ranks are most confident, meaning the top 20% and bottom 20% by absolute distance from the median rank. Add them to the training set with their blended predictions as pseudo targets. Refit the Tanimoto GP on the augmented set with the same sigma2 and predict all test molecules again. The final output is the rank blend of the descriptor LightGBM and this second GP. Use only the seed argument for randomness.
backlog.title: Pseudo-labelling of test molecules for the GP

backlog.spec: Add a k-nearest-neighbour regressor on the Morgan bits with Tanimoto similarity. For each test molecule, take the k=10 most similar training molecules by tanimoto(X_te, X_tr), and use a similarity-weighted average of their rank targets, with weights sim**3. Rank-transform this prediction and blend it with the existing two members using equal thirds, where the rank-blend weights become 0.4 for descriptor LightGBM, 0.3 for GP and 0.3 for kNN. Do not change the GP or the LightGBM.
backlog.title: Third blend member: Tanimoto kNN regression

backlog.spec: The GP branch of train.py uses a pure Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits (tanimoto(X_tr, X_tr)), so it is blind to the physchem descriptors that the LightGBM branch sees. Enrich the kernel: compute an RBF kernel on a small set of standardized descriptors, and multiply it elementwise into the Tanimoto kernel. Concretely, take the descriptor matrix from desc_features, select a handful of interpretable columns by name (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHAcceptors, NumHDonors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3) by looking up their position in Descriptors.descList, standardize them using the training mean and std (guard zero std), and form K_rbf = exp(-gamma * squared euclidean distance) with gamma = 1 / n_selected_features. Use K = K_tanimoto * K_rbf everywhere the Tanimoto kernel is currently used (train-train for choose_sigma2 and gp_mean, test-train for the posterior mean). Keep the rest of the script, including the 0.6/0.4 rank blend, unchanged.
backlog.title: Product kernel of Tanimoto on fingerprints and RBF on descriptors

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM objective from L2 to Huber, with objective='huber' and alpha=0.2, since the rank target is in [0,1]. Keep the rest of the hyperparameters the same (400 trees, lr 0.03, num_leaves 31). The GP member and the rank blend stay unchanged. This tests whether robust loss helps on the rank-transformed target, where the outliers are compressed.
backlog.title: Huber objective for descriptor LightGBM on the rank target

backlog.spec: Compute 5-fold scaffold-grouped out-of-fold LightGBM descriptor predictions on the training set. Fit the Tanimoto GP to the residuals y - oof. Final score is the LightGBM test prediction plus the GP residual prediction, rank-averaged with the existing GP prediction at weight 0.5 versus the current blend. Keep the code compact.
backlog.title: Residual GP on LightGBM out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: In train.py, change the Tanimoto GP Morgan fingerprint settings N_BITS and RADIUS. Try RADIUS=3 and N_BITS=4096 (one change: set RADIUS=3, N_BITS=4096). The descriptor LightGBM is unaffected, since it does not use these settings. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Morgan radius/size sweep for GP

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan bit fingerprint in the GP with a hashed atom-pair fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize=2048, binary via GetFingerprintAsNumPy). Keep tanimoto, choose_sigma2 and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-pair count Tanimoto GP kernel

backlog.spec: train.py returns W_DESC * rankdata(p_desc)/n + (1 - W_DESC) * rankdata(p_fp)/n as its final prediction and never exploits the structure of the test set itself. Add a cheap transductive post-processing step: after forming the final blended score vector p, compute the Morgan-bit Tanimoto similarity matrix S among the test molecules (reuse bit_fingerprints and tanimoto on test_smiles only), zero its diagonal, keep for each test molecule only its 5 largest similarities (set the rest of the row to 0), row-normalize the kept weights, and return rankdata(0.8 * p + 0.2 * (W @ p)) / n where W is that sparse row-normalized matrix. The idea is that chemically near-identical test molecules should receive similar predictions, which denoises the ranking. Keep the weight 0.8/0.2 and k = 5 as fixed module-level constants so they are easy to see.
backlog.title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions over the test-test similarity graph

backlog.spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM with a cosine-decayed learning rate. Use lgb.train with a learning_rate callback that goes from 0.05 to 0.001 over 400 rounds. Save predictions at rounds 200, 300 and 400 using num_iteration, and average these three predictions before ranking. Keep num_leaves 31, subsample 0.8 and colsample 0.5 as they are. Seeds come from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate decay with snapshot averaging in LightGBM

backlog.spec: After the final blended rank vector is computed in fit_predict, smooth it over the test-test chemical similarity graph. Compute the Morgan-bit Tanimoto similarity matrix S between the test molecules with the existing bit_fingerprints and tanimoto helpers, zero its diagonal, and for each test molecule keep only its 5 largest similarities (set the rest of the row to 0). Then return 0.8 * p + 0.2 * (S_knn @ p) / max(S_knn.sum(1), 1e-9), i.e. a single step of neighbour averaging with weights proportional to similarity, applied to the blended rank prediction p. This uses only test SMILES (allowed, they are given to fit_predict) and enforces that near-identical test molecules get near-identical predictions, which can only help a rank metric if the similarity graph is informative. Re-rank the result before returning.
backlog.title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions over test-test similarity

backlog.spec: In train.py the descriptor branch is a single LightGBM (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10) fit with random_state=seed. With subsampling and column sampling at 0.5, a single fit carries noticeable variance that directly enters the 0.6-weighted rank. Replace it with an average of five such models using random_state = seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 (all other hyperparameters identical), rank-transform each model's test prediction, and average those five rank vectors to form p_desc. Keep n_jobs=8 and reduce per-model n_estimators only if the job exceeds about 7 minutes. The GP branch and the final 0.6/0.4 blend stay exactly as they are.
backlog.title: Average the descriptor LightGBM over several seeds

backlog.spec: Replace the 3-value grid in choose_sigma2 with a finer grid of sigma2 in (0.03,0.06,0.1,0.2,0.3,0.5,1.0) and also a kernel amplitude scale chosen from (0.5,1,2) by the same grouped CV Spearman. Then pick the best pair. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Type-II ML GP noise and amplitude

backlog.spec: Currently train.py trains a descriptor LightGBM and a Morgan-bit Tanimoto GP independently on the same rank target and then rank-averages their test predictions with weights 0.6/0.4. Replace this parallel blend with a boosted (sequential) form: first get out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set using a 5-fold scaffold-grouped split (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles as group key, GroupKFold, both already imported), compute the residual r = y_rank minus out-of-fold prediction, then fit the Tanimoto-kernel GP (same bit_fingerprints, tanimoto, choose_sigma2, gp_mean path, but on r instead of y) and predict residuals for the test molecules. Refit the LightGBM on all training data for the test prediction. The final score is rankdata(p_lgbm_full + p_resid_gp) / n. Keep model hyperparameters as they are.
backlog.title: Tanimoto GP on the residuals of the descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace the rank blend with a residual scheme. Fit the descriptor LightGBM with 5-fold GroupKFold on the training molecules, grouped by Murcko scaffold, to get out-of-fold predictions. Compute residuals r = y_rank minus the out-of-fold prediction. Fit the Tanimoto GP (chosen sigma2) on r, using the Morgan bits. For test molecules, the output is the LightGBM prediction from a model fit on all training data plus the GP mean of the residuals, and this sum is then rank-transformed.
backlog.title: Residual GP on out-of-fold descriptor LightGBM predictions

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, build Morgan bit fingerprints for radius in {1, 2, 3} and fpSize in {1024, 2048}. For each of the six combinations, score the GP with choose_sigma2's grouped 5-fold procedure on the training molecules only, using Spearman as the score, and keep the best (radius, size, sigma2) triple for the final GP fit on all training molecules. The test set is never used for the choice. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend as they are.
backlog.title: Inner-CV selection of Morgan radius and bit size for the GP

backlog.spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM with 5 different seeds (seed+i) with subsample and colsample randomness, and average the predictions before rank blending. Reduces variance of the descriptor model.
backlog.title: Multi-seed LightGBM averaging

backlog.spec: Replace the scalar sigma2 in gp_mean with a per-training-molecule noise vector. For each training molecule, compute its mean Tanimoto similarity to its 10 nearest training neighbours (excluding itself). Set noise_i = sigma2 * (1 + c * (1 - density_i)), with c in {0.5, 1.0} chosen by the same grouped inner CV as sigma2. Use np.diag of this vector in place of sigma2 * np.eye in the solve. Test-time predictions use the same formula.
backlog.title: Density-scaled heteroscedastic GP noise

memo: Helped: moving from the RF baseline (about 0.6103) to a rank-averaged blend of descriptor LightGBM plus a fingerprint model (0.5337), then rank-transforming the target (0.5123), then swapping ExtraTrees for a Tanimoto-kernel GP on Morgan bits (0.4971/0.4965; incumbent, mean_adjusted 0.4968 over 2 runs). Did not help: sample weighting, bit filtering, feature selection, LightGBM or CatBoost swaps, stacking, monotone constraints, count or FCFP kernels, multi-kernel sums, MACCS bits, target smoothing, blend-weight search (+0.0060), lipophilicity prior, and LightGBM regularization or tuning. MLP, SVR, kernel ridge and random Fourier features looked good on first runs (0.4879-0.4943) but their replicates were worse. Noise sd is about 0.0070, so gains under that are unreliable. Most of the 40-slot budget has been spent, with 6 aborts from not reading the file first. Next: read the current file first, tune GP noise and Morgan radius/size, and try a replicated MLP or RFF ensemble for diversity.
